svg.title: Choosing a counselling approach
svg.desc: Four stacked bands matching a type of difficulty to the approach usually suited to it: current maintaining patterns to cognitive behavioural work, live memories to EMDR, a nervous system pattern to somatic work, and understanding without change to acceptance and commitment therapy.
svg.text: Which approach tends to fit which problem

text.tspan: Avoidance, a thinking pattern, a habit that has stopped serving you. Structured cognitive behavioural work has the largest
evidence base and usually moves fastest.

svg.text: A memory is still firing in the present

text.tspan: You know intellectually that it is over and your body has not received the update. EMDR is the more direct route;
trauma-focused cognitive work is the alternative with comparable evidence.
The pattern lives in the nervous system rather than in what you understand. Somatic approaches work with tension, breath and
impulse as information rather than as symptoms.

svg.text: You understand it completely and are still stuck

text.tspan: Insight has arrived and nothing changed. ACT targets the struggle rather than the symptom; parts work fits when the experience
Working out which applies is part of the consultation, not a prerequisite for booking one.
